text:
incident-bot: Paging: High error rate and 5xx surge for tenant org=orion in dedicated-pool eu-west-2. Alert: tenant_isolation.alert > 90% errors. Threshold breached at 3333333333
Tom (oncall): ack — investigating. pulling logs now. visible 503 spikes across frontends, spike started ~3333333300 
Maria (SRE): looking at pool telemetry, saw huge KV cache churn and memory pressure on worker nodes in orion-pool-a. CPU fine, but qps+latency align with cache thrash. possible noisy neighbor.
Anita (Eng-runtime): can we drain affected nodes and route traffic to standby pool? if it's KV eviction thrash, flush won't help unless we reduce concurrency per-tenant.
Tom (oncall): starting graceful drain on node g-12 and g-13, switching routing policy to prefer orion-standby (eu-west-2-b). Will hold for 2-3 mins to observe.
Kelly (AM): @Tom @Maria pls keep me posted — Orion leadership is on the line, want minute-by-minute. I told them we have SREs on it.
Maria (SRE): drain commands: ```sh
rctl drain-node --node g-12 --grace 45
rctl drain-node --node g-13 --grace 45
```
Maria (SRE): route update: ```json
{"route":"orion","preferred_pool":"eu-west-2-b"}
``` -> applied at 3333333342
Tom (oncall): after routing change, 503s dropped by ~70% but latency for large prompts still elevated. looks like background KV replication backlog spilled over.
Anita (Eng-runtime): rolling a hotfix to prevent cross-tenant KV eviction. small change to allocator to honor tenant caps. deploying canary to one host now.
Sasha (Product): timeline note: customer saw failures between 3333333300 and 3333333380 (~80s), but some 503s persisted until routing change completed. Need to capture exact error counts for comms.
James (Security): any indicators of malicious activity? traffic patterns look organic; no unusual IPs. marking low risk.
Leo (CS): Orion reports some API errors during a major scheduled batch job; they're escalated internally. They're asking for root cause + mitigation + what permanent change we'll implement.
Maria (SRE): mitigation summary so far: drained two noisy nodes, routed to standby pool, applied temporary per-tenant concurrency caps (limit 20 concurrent requests for orion), canary hotfix to allocator rolled. Error rate back to baseline by 3333333360.
Tom (oncall): marking incident as mitigated at 3333333362. still watching for recurrences.
Anita (Eng-runtime): RCA draft bullets: - Trigger: rapid KV cache churn on dedicated pool caused eviction storms that degraded tail latency and produced 503s for tenant orion. - Root cause: allocator didn't enforce per-tenant cache/concurrency quotas under bursty batch loads, allowing single tenant background jobs to monopolize shared cache working set. - Immediate mitigation: drained nodes, rerouted traffic, applied temporary concurrency cap, canary allocator fix. - Permanent actions: enforce per-tenant cache quotas, add eviction back-pressure, enhance autoscaling to detect cache-thrash patterns, add a dedicated tenant isolation mode for reserved pools.
Kelly (AM): that reads good. Orion will want an exec-friendly one-pager with impact window, number of failed requests, user-visible effects, and proposed credits per SLA.
Sasha (Product): suggested customer comm draft (short): "We identified a cache eviction storm in your reserved pool that caused request errors and increased latency between 3333333300–3333333362. We've applied mitigations and are implementing changes to prevent recurrence. Our recommended credit is one week of reserved throughput for March. More details attached." Thoughts?
James (Security): legal/infosec review not required but include what data scoping we checked (no cross-tenant data leakage observed).
Tom (oncall): attaching quick metrics snippet: ```
errors(orion)/minute: [0,0,12,85,200,150,30,2,0]
latency_p95_ms: [120,130,400,900,1500,800,200,130,120]
``` from 3333333280–3333333380
Maria (SRE): total failed requests ~3.8k during window. peak impacted requests from large-batch job.
Leo (CS): Orion-facing timeline draft ready. I'll propose immediate comm that acknowledges outage, explains cause in plain terms, lists mitigations, and offers meeting for exec Q&A.
Kelly (AM): on credits — legal suggests start with proposed credit calc: (monthly reserved fee * downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) then cap to negotiated SLA floor. For orion that's roughly 0.23% of month => suggest offering 5% monthly credit as good will? open to discussion.
Sasha (Product): 5% seems high relative to actual minutes. propose 1 week of reserved throughput or equivalent billing credit; aligns with prior enterprise precedents.
James (Security): confirm we have audit logs to show no customer data access beyond normal, add that sentence to comms.
Anita (Eng-runtime): action items I will own: 1) push allocator fix to prod for all dedicated pools by EOD (+ rollback plan). 2) add per-tenant cache quota enforcement PR by EOW. 3) run chaos test for KV eviction patterns.
Maria (SRE): I will create post-incident dashboard and upload metrics + sample logs. ETA 4 hours.
Tom (oncall): I'll file the incident ticket in JIRA and tag for RCA. Ticket: INF-9876. Will include timeline and commands.
Leo (CS): I'll loop in Orion CSM and schedule a 30-minute run-through with their engineering leads tomorrow.
Kelly (AM): I'll draft exec note and propose the monetary credit option: 1-week reserved throughput (equivalent $X) and offer a technical deep-dive. Putting a soft hold on final credit until legal confirms.
Sasha (Product): can we add a new runbook step for "force route to standby pool" so CS/AM can quickly apply if similar event hits customer reserved pools?
Tom (oncall): good idea — adding to runbook and creating a one-click route toggle in console backlog.
James (Security): no further action from security side. I'll sign off once comms include data scope statement.
Anita (Eng-runtime): leaving notes for postmortem: reproducer script, PR numbers, perf tests. Will add estimated ETA for each permanent action in the RCA doc.
Maria (SRE): final operational note: we observed a correlated background job from orion at 3333333295 that triggered a heavy load. recommend customers be advised about large scheduled jobs hitting reserved pools and we add guidance to best-practice docs.
Leo (CS): thanks everyone. I'll post the customer-facing timeline and draft email by EOD for review.
Kelly (AM): thanks — ping me when comms ready, I'll take customer call. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident 3333333333 marked mitigated at 3333333362, postmortem required. Reminder: please fill in RCA template: https://redwood.internal/rca-template
